text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

---Den Danske Bank's Danske Data unit may replace the outgoing BG Bank in the SDC banking data alliance, the bank believes that joining the network could save it millions of crowns in operating costs.
---Tele Danmark is charging business customers excessive tariffs, in defiance of two orders from telecoms watchdog Telestyrelsen.
---Danish banking shares are trading at a significant discount to Swedish paper, because the Swedish banks have become more international.

--- Den Danske Bank is playing a dual role in the Phoenix Contractors takeover saga, acting both as advisor for bidder Icopal and as banker and shareholder in Phoenix, but the bank says that the two sides are kept strictly divided.
--- Economists believe that January's 3,500 rise in unemployment is a short-term phenomenon and not the start of a trend
--- The tax ministry has closed a legal loophole which allowed life insurance firms to avoid paying tax on some securities gains by splitting themselves into several smaller companies.
--- German state-owned Landesbank Schleswig-Holstein plans to use its new Copenhagen branch as a bridgehead for expansion in Scandinavia.
--- Rieber and Son says it will buy Phoenix Contractors, sending a strong signal that it will raise its offer before Friday's 1500 GMT deadline.
--- Seven out of 10 Conservative voters would rather have Liberal leader Uffe Ellemann-Jensen as head of a coalition government than one of their own party chiefs.

--- Recent strikes by public sector employees indicate dissatisfaction with botched attempts to link pay to productivity and a more fundamental appraisal of the system is needed, a labour market analyst says.
